correctness.rationale: Exact scalar and simplex normalization from the source operator; each alpha=1/2 pair exchange is a rank-one orthogonal projector on the centered 2-plane. The three unit axes have off-diagonal Gram entries -1/2. Their product gives the exact signed path identity, the iid indicator counting proves Binomial(n-1,2/3) with independence of first pair, and the 3-state no-loop chain gives exact terminal pair probabilities. Averaging yields every q>0 moment. SLLN and CLT apply to iid indicators only under nonzero first-step projection. Exact-rational checker reproduces every 3^n calendar for n=1,...,8 and q=2,4 moments.

originality.rationale: The original family and autonomous trajectory properties are previously published, and all general mean-square gossip estimates are acknowledged. The assessed increment is the finite-time signed rank-one product law including exact binomial multiplier, joint terminal orientation, arbitrary real positive moments and quenched CLT within a nonlinear four-species model. Broad semantic searches and relevant primary source inspections found no dominating statement; inaccessible source portions and possible equivalent three-agent gossip formulations remain a concrete priority risk, not a demonstrated novelty certificate.
residual_risks: The full texts of the 2020 permutation-operator article and 2023 follow-up were unavailable, and their abstracts alone do not certify noncoverage.
The full classical three-agent gossip literature may contain an equivalent joint binomial statement or a general theorem subsuming it.
A single search index or disciplinary partition cannot establish global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The triangle is the smallest fully connected population-composition exchange geometry with different, noncommuting rank-one averaging projections. The result classifies an entire finite-time stochastic evolution rather than just its expected contraction, including signed orientation, all positive noninteger moment orders and a provably different typical-versus-annealed decay exponent. This natural limiting projection parameter produces a tractable stochastic transport invariant useful for understanding transient composition variability in four-species quadratic populations. The result does not claim a universal high-dimensional theorem.
